messages:
mina: Heads up — seeing a cluster of nodes in us-east1 lose GPU partitions after tonight's driver bump. ~12 nodes report no MIG slices.
james: Which driver/CUDA combo was deployed?
mina: Driver 535.54 + CUDA 12.3 from the automated rollout at ~01:10 UTC.
olga: Any logs or quick `nvidia-smi` output?
mina: Paste: ```
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee)
# but no MIG devices listed

$ nvidia-smi mig -lgc
Failed to query MIG devices: NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED
``` 
mina: Daemonset on the node reports: "MIG profile restore failed: incompatible driver / unexpected NVML response". Some ML pods hit "failed to create device handle".
kai: I noticed on a handful of those hosts the PCI bus IDs changed (kernel probe sequence altered), which results in device mapping shift. Scheduler still expects old device ids/labels so pods can't find the allocated slice.
james: Could be NVML ABI change in 535.54 + our kernel/CRI combo; NVML returns different enumeration and our device-plugin assumes stable UUID mapping.
olga: Is this limited to us-east1?
mina: Mostly us-east1-a/c. west and europe pools were on the previous driver and look fine. Rolling one node back to 534.x restored MIG partitions immediately.
kai: For remediation we should: 1) pause rollout 2) roll back affected pools 3) re-run MIG profile restore + reboot if needed. Quick commands I ran: ```
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-534
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
sudo nvidia-smi -L
sudo nvidia-smi mig -i 0 -cgi 19,19,19,19 -C  # (example create command)
``` 
james: Opened INC-5421 and pinged NVIDIA support with NVML traces and `dmesg` from an impacted host. I've also added a rollback task to the rollout runbook and paused the rest of the 535.54 jobs. :eyes:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback triggered for pool "gpu-pool-us-east1" — 3 nodes rolled back so far, remaining 9 in progress.
olga: Action item: add a preflight check to the driver upgrade playbook to validate MIG enumeration via NVML (`nvidia-smi mig -L`) and confirm device-plugin can map by PCI bus ID or fallback to PCI address matching.
kai: Also we need to update our device-plugin to tolerate remapped UUIDs — fallback to matching by PCI bus ID and, if available, compute a stable ID from kernel sysfs paths.
mina: For now I set a scheduling override to move critical jobs off the affected nodes and I'm draining the rest one-by-one while rolling them back. Will keep updating INC-5421. :thumbsup:
james: Good. After rollback we should run a canary upgrade with the exact kernel + driver pairing and exercise MIG create/restore paths before mass rollout.
mina: I'll capture the node-level NVML traces and share in the ticket. Thanks everyone.
